narrative: Material PL2__ME34E7A1 shows smooth, consistent daily demand (CV=0.415) with no detectable trend across 96 working-day observations. Lead times are moderately variable (CV=0.440, mean 2.58 days), contributing meaningfully to combined lead-time demand uncertainty. A continuous-review (r,Q) policy was selected to exploit the stable demand signal while buffering against combined demand and lead-time volatility. The EOQ-driven order quantity (268,543) far exceeds the MOQ and delivers a 73% cost reduction versus the current MOQ-only policy.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Smooth, high-frequency demand with 100% non-zero fraction and moderate lead time variability makes a continuous-review (r, Q) policy optimal — it triggers replenishment precisely at the reorder point without excess periodic review overhead.
research_insights.boundary_risk: None — EOQ (268,543) plus safety stock (45,827) = 314,370 units, which is 72.4% of max storage capacity (434,252). Sufficient headroom exists for demand surges.
